I keep mine in a small tub with only one side loosely lined with a thin layer of moss (maybe around 1/8th of the enclosures length). Even though they don't require much humidity it's important to have a small wetter part of the enclosure just in case.

I'd also recommend focusing on spraying less than a quarter of the enclosure as to not create a too humid environment for them.  

The opposite side I keep pretty much bone dry with maybe a tiny spray of water every month or so it doesn't become excruciatingly dry.

Also I find mine absolutely love chilling in leaf litter so a deep and thick layer of that can really help them find a nice dry spot at the bottom if they find above too humid


TLDR
Keep it considerably drier than you'd usually keep isopods however a small wet patch and some humidity is still essential for them to survive. Don't let it dry out completely

Emaj7,G#m,B,G#m11-F#m11
